confucius-01.translation: Isn't it a joy to learn and return to what you have learned?
confucius-01.note: Learning becomes yours when you revisit it and put it into practice.

confucius-02.translation: Isn't it a delight when friends come from far away?
confucius-02.note: A friend who makes the journey to see you is a reason for joy.

confucius-03.translation: Revisit what you know, and discover something new.
confucius-03.note: Looking again at an old lesson can reveal a meaning you missed.

confucius-04.translation: Know what you know, and admit what you don't. That is understanding.
confucius-04.note: Honesty about the limits of your knowledge is part of wisdom.

confucius-05.translation: Among the people I walk with, someone always has something to teach me.
confucius-05.note: You can learn from the people around you, whatever their role or age.

confucius-06.translation: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you.
confucius-06.note: Before you act, imagine how it would feel to be on the receiving end.

confucius-07.translation: Worry less about being understood, and more about understanding others.
confucius-07.note: Turn your attention from getting recognition to noticing other people.

confucius-08.translation: A person of character is more than a tool for a single task.
confucius-08.note: Grow your judgment and character, rather than defining yourself by one useful skill.

confucius-09.translation: Each day, I examine myself in three ways.
confucius-09.note: In the Analects, Zengzi asks whether he has been faithful, trustworthy and practiced what he learned.

confucius-10.translation: Only in the cold do we see how long the pine and cypress keep their leaves.
confucius-10.note: Difficult times reveal the qualities that remain steady within a person.

confucius-11.translation: I guide those eager to understand, and help those struggling to express a thought.
confucius-11.note: A teacher can help most when a learner is already reaching for an answer.

confucius-12.translation: Good character does not stand alone; it draws others near.
confucius-12.note: Living with care and integrity can bring you people who value the same things.

confucius-13.translation: A person of character is at ease; a small-minded person is always troubled.
confucius-13.note: A wider concern for what is right can loosen the grip of everyday worries.

confucius-14.translation: To make a mistake and refuse to correct it is the real mistake.
confucius-14.note: What matters is not being perfect, but being willing to change.

confucius-15.translation: Firmness, resolve, simplicity and modest speech bring us close to kindness.
confucius-15.note: A caring character is built through steady actions, not polished words alone.

confucius-16.translation: Do not worry about having no position. Work on what makes you fit for one.
confucius-16.note: Focus on becoming ready for responsibility rather than chasing a title.

confucius-17.translation: Without thought for the future, trouble will soon come near.
confucius-17.note: Making a little room for tomorrow can prevent problems today.

confucius-18.translation: A person of character looks for what is right; a small-minded person looks for gain.
confucius-18.note: Ask whether a choice is fair before asking what you can get from it.

confucius-19.translation: When it comes to doing what is humane, do not hold back even for your teacher.
confucius-19.note: Respect does not mean waiting for someone else to do the caring thing first.

confucius-20.translation: Aim for the Way, stand on good character, rely on kindness, and explore the arts.
confucius-20.note: A full life joins a sense of direction, moral care and the pleasure of learning skills.

laozi-01.translation: A way put into words is not the lasting Way.
laozi-01.note: Words can point toward experience, but cannot contain all of it.

laozi-02.translation: Understanding others is wisdom; understanding yourself is clarity.
laozi-02.note: Looking inward matters just as much as being good at reading other people.

laozi-03.translation: The highest goodness is like water.
laozi-03.note: Water helps life without competing, and flows to places others avoid.

laozi-04.translation: A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath your feet.
laozi-04.note: A distant goal starts with the step you can take right now.

laozi-05.translation: Those who know when they have enough are rich.
laozi-05.note: Feeling wealthy can come from contentment, not just from owning more.

laozi-06.translation: The soft and yielding overcome the hard and strong.
laozi-06.note: Flexibility can outlast a force that knows only how to resist.

laozi-07.translation: The greatest skill can look awkward.
laozi-07.note: Deep skill need not show itself through decoration or display.

laozi-08.translation: Good fortune leans on trouble; trouble hides within good fortune.
laozi-08.note: What seems good or bad can change, so avoid judging a whole situation too quickly.

laozi-09.translation: Those who know do not talk; those who talk do not know.
laozi-09.note: The sharp contrast invites us to question whether words are replacing real understanding.

laozi-10.translation: Nothing in the world is softer or weaker than water.
laozi-10.note: The wider passage uses water to show how gentleness can wear down what is hard.

laozi-11.translation: Learning adds something each day; following the Way lets something go each day.
laozi-11.note: Gathering knowledge and letting go of needless effort are different kinds of growth.

laozi-12.translation: Act without forcing, and nothing is left undone.
laozi-12.note: This is not a call to do nothing, but to act without pushing against everything.

laozi-13.translation: A great vessel takes time to finish.
laozi-13.note: Important abilities may develop slowly. This follows the wording of the supplied text.

laozi-14.translation: Too many words soon run out. Better to keep your center.
laozi-14.note: Constant explaining can drain you; a steady inner balance may help more.

laozi-15.translation: To understand what endures is clarity.
laozi-15.note: Look for the steady patterns within a world that keeps changing.

laozi-16.translation: Those who overcome themselves are strong.
laozi-16.note: Working with your own habits can take more strength than defeating someone else.

laozi-17.translation: Take as much care at the end as you did at the beginning.
laozi-17.note: Keep paying attention when a task feels almost finished.

laozi-18.translation: A tree you can barely embrace grows from a tiny shoot.
laozi-18.note: Large things begin small. Give small beginnings the care they need.

laozi-19.translation: Finish the work without holding on to the credit.
laozi-19.note: You can do something well without making the achievement your whole identity.

laozi-20.translation: By not showing off, you become clear to others.
laozi-20.note: Let the quality of your actions speak instead of constantly drawing attention to yourself.

sunzi-01.translation: Know the other side and yourself, and a hundred battles need not put you in danger.
sunzi-01.note: Good judgment needs an honest view of both your situation and the other side's.

sunzi-02.translation: Bring the opposing army to yield without fighting.
sunzi-02.note: The surrounding passage values reaching an outcome without the destruction of battle.

sunzi-03.translation: Warfare is a way of deception.
sunzi-03.note: This describes military strategy. It is not advice to deceive people in everyday relationships.

sunzi-04.translation: Strike where they are unprepared; appear where they do not expect you.
sunzi-04.note: In a military setting, preparation includes noticing gaps in the other side's expectations.

sunzi-05.translation: In war, value victory rather than a long campaign.
sunzi-05.note: A conflict that drags on drains resources and harms the people involved.

sunzi-06.translation: A skilled commander draws others into position, rather than being drawn by them.
sunzi-06.note: Try to shape a situation thoughtfully instead of only reacting to pressure.

sunzi-07.translation: Know the weather and the ground, and victory can be complete.
sunzi-07.note: Understanding people is not enough; timing and surroundings also matter.

sunzi-08.translation: An army has no fixed pattern, just as water has no fixed shape.
sunzi-08.note: A good plan changes with the conditions rather than clinging to one form.

sunzi-09.translation: Move swiftly like the wind; move slowly with the stillness of a forest.
sunzi-09.note: Match your pace to the situation. Speed is useful only when it fits.

sunzi-10.translation: Knowledge in advance cannot be obtained from spirits.
sunzi-10.note: The passage calls for information from people, rather than guesses or supernatural signs.

sunzi-11.translation: Winning every battle is not the highest kind of skill.
sunzi-11.note: Avoiding the need for a fight can be better than repeatedly winning one.

sunzi-12.translation: The best strategy is to defeat the other side's plans.
sunzi-12.note: Sun Tzu places disrupting a strategy above meeting armies in battle.

sunzi-13.translation: War is a matter of great importance to a state.
sunzi-13.note: The opening treats war as a grave decision, not something to enter lightly.

sunzi-14.translation: Those who know when to fight and when not to fight will win.
sunzi-14.note: Choosing whether to enter a conflict comes before choosing how to fight it.

sunzi-15.translation: Place them where they could perish, and only then will they survive.
sunzi-15.note: This is a historical military claim about desperate situations, not advice to endanger yourself or others.

sunzi-16.translation: A skilled commander avoids an enemy whose spirit is sharp.
sunzi-16.note: Rather than meeting peak force head-on, consider when the situation will change.

sunzi-17.translation: Wait nearby for those who travel far; wait rested for those who are tired.
sunzi-17.note: Preparation and conserving energy can matter more than rushing into action.

sunzi-18.translation: Speed is central to the nature of warfare.
sunzi-18.note: In the military context of the passage, an opportunity can disappear if action comes too late.

sunzi-19.translation: A commander needs wisdom, trustworthiness, kindness, courage and discipline.
sunzi-19.note: Leadership is not only about force. Care for people and reliability matter too.

sunzi-20.translation: A winning army secures the conditions for victory before seeking battle.
sunzi-20.note: Build a sound position before committing yourself, rather than relying on hope afterward.
